verdict: AVOID new Ankleshwar chemicals/dyes exposure; only exception-led working-capital facilities to compliant, integrated exporters with verified pass-through, secured on current assets and checked monthly for consent/CETP status.
title: Ankleshwar Chemicals, Dyes & Intermediates: a note to the credit manager
narrative: **The data pack gives AVOID 43 [D], and the local news direction is Worse, so new Ankleshwar dye/intermediate exposure is not a normal-terms yes.** National IIP for NIC 20 is -0.5% YoY and -1.2% Apr-to-date, bank credit is +20.7% YoY versus that output, a +21.9 pp gap, and Brent is $113/bbl [D]. Local costs are moving the other way: May-2026 reporting shows fuel, freight and crude-linked inputs higher, production costs 12–15%, benzene/toluene/solvents up to 20%, container transport from Mumbai to Ankleshwar from Rs 34,000–36,000 to Rs 39,000–42,000, and monthly transport up to Rs 5 lakh [3]. So when a proposal lands, check for a written pass-through clause for fuel and raw material; if absent, ask for recent price-revision letters and decline where gross margin is already compressed.

**A dye/intermediate unit is a batch converter: imported crude-derived benzene, toluene and solvents go through multi-step reactions into dyes and intermediates, then ship to textile, leather, paper and ink buyers.** Gujarat is close to 75% of dye and intermediate output, with Ankleshwar among the main centres [2]; that is an industry estimate, not current audited data. Bharuch district contributes nearly 19% of India's chemical exports and Ankleshwar GIDC is described as one of Asia's largest industrial estates [3]. Cash is not made at the reactor: it is made after compliant effluent treatment, batch approval and export receivable collection. Value sits in buyer approvals and consent to operate; cash sits in inventory and receivables, and capex sits in reactors, utilities and ETP/OCEMS. Where capacity, product mix, ETP capacity or CETP membership are not in the file, collect from customer.

**The local cost shock is real and recent: May-2026 reporting shows Gujarat chemical units facing higher fuel, freight and imported crude-derived input costs [3].** That local source predates today, so refresh fuel bills and freight invoices before sanction. The regulatory backdrop is older but structural: dyes and intermediates are in CPCB's 17 highly polluting categories, Red category, with OCEMS directions from 2014/2015 and closure directions reported in 2018 [1]. A unit without valid consent, OCEMS connectivity and CETP dues clearance is not a lending candidate, whatever its order book. The rating page for Kesar Petroproducts is date unknown and gives no financial detail [8]; collect from customer and do not use it as comfort.

**Peers are not uniformly weak: Shanghai-listed Zhejiang Longsheng reports 26Q3 dye volume and price up, with disperse dye average price 28.07 yuan/kg YoY +74% and reactive dye 37.36 yuan/kg YoY +68% [5][6].** Aarti Industries reports Q2 FY27 volume up over 30%, revenue ₹3,887 crore +73% YoY and record quarterly EBITDA ₹418 crore, helped by export demand and pass-through of raw material costs [7]. The lesson is to back units that can pass through costs and have export/qualified-customer traction, not every small dye unit in the cluster. Peer strength is not local proof; use it to choose borrower type.
## Who to pursue and how to grow safely

**Pursue integrated exporters and specialty/intermediate makers with own ETP/OCEMS, documented buyer restricted-substance compliance, and contracts that pass through fuel and raw material.** Avoid standalone commodity dye units dependent on a CETP, imported intermediates and diesel-based power, unless the promoter injects fresh equity and the bank gets cash cover. Structure as working-capital limits against pari passu charge on current assets, promoter guarantee, escrow of export receivables and LC-backed sales where available. Take every month: stock and book-debt statement, debtor ageing, GST returns against sales register, export shipment/LC evidence, power and fuel bills, OCEMS data and CETP payment receipts. Covenant on current ratio, DSCR and no dividend; if any consent notice or CETP arrears appear, freeze limits.

**Watch the cash conversion, not the order book: rising inventory days, stretched debtor ageing, GST-sales mismatch, unpaid power bills and CETP arrears precede default in this trade.** If freight or fuel surcharge is not being recovered in invoices, ask for customer price letters; if missing, reduce exposure. A consent notice, OCEMS gap or closure direction is an exit trigger, not a negotiation point. Where the unit cannot show buyer compliance for azo/restricted substances, collect from customer and decline until documented.
